clue.text: It's not well organised to keep a pet in the pig's house

indicators.note: the sty is made to hold the pet within its walls, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a sty is where a pig is kept
a cat is a typical household pet

explanation.surface: Someone complains it is badly arranged to house a pet in a pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatty is British informal for scatterbrained and disorganised.

clue.text: Pus got in via the drainpipe

indicators.note: the letters travel by way of a new route, so they are rearranged before arriving

parts.note: fodder
fodder
fodder

explanation.surface: Infected matter has found its way into the house through the drainpipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'via' is a loose anagram signal: the letters of PUS GOT IN are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Spouting is a British name for guttering and downpipes that carry rainwater.

clue.text: A couple of pages by a top journalist without everybody being horrified!

indicators.note: old sense of 'outside': the first group of letters sits around the word for everybody

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page, so two pages are PP
the editor, ED, is the senior journalist on a paper
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A sheet or two from a leading writer, none of it for general consumption, leaves readers shocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; a journalist's top is an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Appalled is a synonym: filled with horror and dismay.

clue.text: Fewer than a dozen looked around on the cutter

parts.note: ten is one figure short of twelve
to have looked around is to have seen, i.e. saw

explanation.surface: Ten people peered at a cutting tool.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenon saw is a fine-toothed carpenter's saw for cutting joints.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a tool that cuts, so it is a cutter.

clue.text: Find that the record has finished

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
over means ended

explanation.surface: Someone learns that a vinyl album has reached its last track.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something is to come upon or uncover it, a synonym.

clue.text: It's conceivable to think in untidy lab

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed within the verb for think

parts.note: to imagine is to think of

indicators.note: an untidy room is jumbled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone muses that it's believable a scientist might ponder in a messy laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidy' scrambles the laboratory's short name into ABL; 'in' sets that inside the verb; 'It's' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean able to be pictured in the mind, synonyms.

clue.text: Firm man needed, to be convincing

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
gent is short for gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A company needs a persuasive person.
explanation.definitionFit: A cogent argument is persuasive, a synonym.

clue.text: Salesman drove in the point somehow

indicators.note: the compass letter is set inside the rearranged word
done in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A salesman forcefully made his argument in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges DROVE into VEDOR, and 'in' places N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendor is someone who sells, a synonym.

clue.text: Tell how the Spanish speed around!

indicators.note: the word for speed is spread about the Spanish article

parts.note: rate means speed, as in a rate of knots
el is the Spanish word for 'the'

explanation.surface: An instruction to describe how fast Spanish people travel.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell or narrate it.

clue.text: Short plant with purple flowers alternatively, long!

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
to pine is to long for something

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a small purple-flowered plant, or perhaps a tall one.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpine is a stonecrop, a low-growing sedum with purple flower clusters.

clue.text: Alarming perhaps when a member has to fight for this seat

definitions.text: when a member has to fight for this seat
definitions.note: a phrase describing a seat; the answer is the noun used for such a seat

indicators.note: signals the letters could be some other arrangement

explanation.surface: It is worrying for an MP to have to battle to hold their constituency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ALARMING. A MARGINAL is a parliamentary seat held by a small majority.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat won by a narrow majority is easily lost, so the sitting MP must campaign hard.

clue.text: Thanks given temporarily for innate ability

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
lent means handed over for a while, to be returned

explanation.surface: Gratitude expressed briefly for a natural gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Talent is a natural gift or aptitude, a synonym.

clue.text: It gives directions on how to put a name at the bottom of a letter

parts.words: put a name at the bottom
parts.note: to sign a document is to write one's name at its foot
post is mail, letters

explanation.surface: Advice on how to end a letter with your signature.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside post with arms pointing the way to places.

clue.text: Half hearted rule Tories have broken

indicators.note: something broken is smashed, so these letters are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A political jibe that a feeble government's rule has been wrecked by the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: TORIES are members of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone irresolute lacks determination, so is lukewarm and wavering.

clue.text: Want an opportunity to take a holiday

explanation.surface: Someone tired longs for some time off.
explanation.definitionFit: Need means want and a break is a chance; a break is also a short vacation, so both readings fit.

clue.text: It's a dim thing to be out so late

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says it's foolish to stay out at such a late hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DIM THING; 'It's a' and 'to be' join the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve at night is a very late hour.

clue.text: Worried about nothing in a strange design

indicators.note: the zero letter is put inside the rearranged phrase
something strange is odd, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone frets over trivia in an odd pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges DESIGN into GNISED, and 'in' puts O inside it after the A; 'about' only joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Agonised means tormented by worry or anguish.

clue.text: One's given a guarantee, I see, following the concert

indicators.note: the words I see come after the concert in the answer

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms

explanation.surface: Someone after a concert reports they have been given an assurance.
explanation.walkthrough: The PROMS are a famous summer season of BBC concerts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A promisee is the person to whom a promise is made.

clue.text: He might jog one's memory, like Quasimodo perhaps

explanation.surface: A man who reminds people, compared to the hunchback of Notre-Dame.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rings a bell prompts a memory; Quasimodo rang the bells of Notre-Dame.

clue.text: Uses influence to transplant

explanation.surface: Someone pulls strings to move a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Graft is corruption through influence; to graft is also to transplant tissue or shoots.

clue.text: So blue about her crumpled chemise

indicators.note: crumpled means crushed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone feels so down about her wrinkled undergarment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumpled' rearranges SO BLUE; 'about her' joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemise is a loose shirt-like garment for a woman, like a blouse.

clue.text: Some might try to bag a direct flight to Moroccan resort

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Travellers try to book a nonstop flight to North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in b(AG A DIR)ect.
explanation.definitionFit: Agadir is a seaside resort city on Morocco's Atlantic coast.

clue.text: One girl I converted to the faith

indicators.note: changed into a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young woman has been brought into a creed.
explanation.definitionFit: A religion is a system of faith and worship.

clue.text: Soon, what is mine will be returned, by someone whose name I don't know

definitions.text: someone whose name I don't know

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

indicators.note: sending something back turns it round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: my is the possessive of I

explanation.surface: A stranger promises to give back my possessions shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: An anonym is a person whose name is unknown, an anonymous person.

clue.text: Ascertained that they were away from home

explanation.surface: Someone discovered a family was not in.
explanation.definitionFit: To have found out is to have discovered; read literally, people found to be out are not at home.

clue.text: Gives out, for example, directions about the way

indicators.note: the compass letters go around the abbreviation for road

parts.note: E and S are compass directions, east and south
St, street, is a way or road

explanation.surface: A guide hands over instructions on the route.
explanation.definitionFit: To egest is to discharge or excrete from the body.

clue.text: Give pike to the fellows who fought hand to hand

definitions.note: a relative clause describing soldiers; the answer is the plural noun for them

parts.note: a pike is a long spear
men are fellows

explanation.surface: An order to arm the soldiers with long weapons for close combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers armed with spears fought at close quarters.

clue.text: Dog set about the suet pudding

indicators.note: about here means around in a muddle, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog sets upon a heavy pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy, filling food such as a steamed suet pudding.
